brief.subject: Wealthy-earner tax votes advance in California and Colorado
brief.headline: State Tax Votes on High Earners Advance as Supreme Court Takes Up Distilling Ban
brief.dek: California and Colorado tax measures move forward, the Supreme Court reviews a federal distilling ban, and a film credit push hits the lame duck.
brief.lede: Voters in California and Colorado are weighing higher taxes on top earners. Colorado's highest court just cleared the way for its measure to proceed.

sections.heading: High-Earner Tax Measures Move Forward
bullets: Colorado's Supreme Court threw out a suit to void the vote on Amendment 87, a tax hike on the wealthiest residents.
California's Proposition 3 would make higher rates permanent above $371,000 for singles and $742,000 for couples.
Prop 3 looks likely to pass, while California's separate billionaire wealth tax is struggling.
Owners of some top California sports teams would face the wealth tax if voters approve it.

sections.heading: Supreme Court Tests Federal Taxing Power
bullets: The Supreme Court will hear a challenge to a 158-year-old federal ban on home distilling.
The core question is whether the ban goes beyond Congress's power to tax.
The ruling could clarify how far federal tax authority reaches into regulating activity.

sections.heading: Film Tax Credit Pushed in Lame Duck
bullets: A bipartisan group is pressing to pass a proposed federal film tax credit before the 119th Congress ends.
Only weeks remain in the session, so the proposal faces a tight window.

sections.heading: Year-End Payroll and Rental Sales
bullets: Many errors that complicate the final 2026 payroll close have already occurred, so reviewing records now matters.
Small landlords selling long-term rentals can lower taxable gain with documented improvements.
Missing improvement records can leave landlords paying tax on a larger gain than necessary.

items.title: Centuries-Old Whiskey Tax Law Faces New Supreme Court Challenge
items.snippet: The U.S. Supreme Court will weigh whether a 158-year-old federal ban on home distilling exceeds Congress's taxing power, a dispute rooted in America's earliest debates over federal authority and revenue enforcement.

items.title: While Billionaire Tax Flounders, Another Progressive Tax in California is Looking Likely
items.snippet: Proposition 3 is a tax measure that would make higher income tax rates permanent for single people who earn more than $371,000 or couples who earn more than $742,000.

items.title: Proposed Billionaire Tax Could Impact California Sports Teams
items.snippet: The billionaires targeted by the wealth tax on the November ballot include owners of some of California's top sports teams and, among them, there will be winners and losers if voters approve the measure.

items.title: Backers of Federal Film Tax Credit Seek Action in Lame-Duck Session
items.snippet: With just weeks to go before the end of the 119th Congress, lawmakers and advocates are making a bipartisan push to get a proposed federal film tax credit over the finish line.

items.title: 5 Key Steps for the 2026 Year-End Payroll Close
items.snippet: The final payroll of 2026 may be weeks away, but many of the mistakes that can complicate year-end have already happened.

items.title: Colorado Supreme Court Rejects Lawsuit Seeking to Stop Income Tax Measure
items.snippet: The Colorado Supreme Court on Friday shot down an attempt to nullify the vote on Amendment 87, allowing the proposal to raise taxes on the state’s wealthiest residents to proceed.
